failure_pattern: A misconfiguration in the signup service caused increased latency, leading to intermittent timeouts and degraded performance for new account creation across multiple Atlassian cloud products.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated health checks and alerting for signup latency; enforce circuit breakers and rate limiting; validate configuration changes through automated tests; add automated rollback on deployment failures; monitor third‑party dependencies and set up fallback mechanisms

symptoms: Service disruption for customers in us-west-1
failure_pattern: During a network migration, the DNS record for the service was not updated to point to the new network segment. When the old network stack was removed, traffic still attempted to reach the old segment, causing failures in media handling and build services across multiple Atlassian products.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated verification that DNS records are updated before decommissioning old stacks; add checks to ensure no customer traffic is served from old stack; incorporate blue/green deployment with thorough verification; add steps to identify associated DNS records during network migration; enforce pre-decommission traffic monitoring

original_source: Performance issues and outages with Cloud products
symptoms: inability for new customers to sign up
failure_pattern: An internal infrastructure component malfunctioned, causing performance degradation and outages across multiple Atlassian Cloud products, leading to slow loading, login failures, and new customer sign-up issues.
mitigation_principle: Implement health checks and automated failover for internal infrastructure components; add monitoring and alerting for performance metrics; conduct regular configuration reviews and change management; perform load testing and capacity planning; enforce rollback procedures for infrastructure changes

original_source: Sign-ups, Product Activation, and Billing not working
failure_pattern: A misconfigured authentication token service caused the sign‑up, product activation, and billing APIs to reject requests, leading to a cascading failure that affected all cloud customers.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated configuration validation; add health checks for critical services; monitor key metrics; use canary deployments for changes; roll back quickly if anomalies detected

symptoms: failed sign‑in, signup, profile retrieval, password reset
failure_pattern: A misconfigured rate limit in an internal core service caused 429 errors; retry logic multiplied the load, triggering a cascading failure across dependent authentication and user‑profile services, which resulted in widespread login and signup failures.
mitigation_principle: Audit and adjust rate limits; implement exponential backoff for retries; perform load testing on complex service interactions; reduce cross‑service dependencies; enable unauthenticated support channels; improve incident notification processes

original_source: Degraded experience for Atlassian Intelligence features
failure_pattern: An increase in the failure rate of the OpenAI API caused higher error responses to the Atlassian Intelligence service, leading to degraded experience across Confluence, Jira, Trello, Bitbucket, and Atlas.
mitigation_principle: Implement retry logic with exponential backoff; add circuit breaker to isolate third‑party failures; monitor third‑party API health and set alerts; maintain fallback mode for AI features; coordinate with third‑party provider for SLA and incident response

original_source: Forge Function Invocations outage impacting Smartlinks
failure_pattern: Forge Invocations experienced an 8‑minute outage from 03:05:13 to 03:13:27 UTC, causing Smart Links to fail during that period.
mitigation_principle: 1. Implement redundant instances for critical services; 2. Add health‑check endpoints and automated failover; 3. Set up real‑time monitoring and alerting for service availability; 4. Conduct post‑mortem reviews to identify root causes.

original_source: Atlassian's cross product user search service is currently degraded.
failure_pattern: A burst of computationally intensive operations targeting the same customer data set overloaded the clustered database, exhausting memory and causing the user search service to become unresponsive, leading to delayed or failed searches across multiple Atlassian cloud products.
mitigation_principle: Implement queuing for heavy operations; fine‑tune clustered database settings to mitigate resource exhaustion.

failure_pattern: A configuration error in the product purchasing service caused the provisioning process to hang, resulting in long waiting pages or error pages for customers attempting to add new products. The issue was identified and the configuration was corrected, restoring normal operation.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated health checks for provisioning services; add circuit breaker patterns; perform configuration validation before deployment; monitor provisioning latency; create rollback plan for config changes

failure_pattern: During a scheduled security uplift, an automated process mistakenly deleted active DNS domain names used for internal service-to-service communication, causing DNS resolution failures across all cloud services, which led to widespread service disruptions and performance degradation until the deployment was rolled back.
mitigation_principle: Implement canary checks for system availability; establish faster rollback procedures; enforce stricter change control for infrastructure modifications; centralize DNS management with stricter access controls

failure_pattern: A misconfiguration in the backend service caused authentication and user management features to fail, preventing users from accessing certain admin portal functionalities during the incident window.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated configuration validation; add health checks for feature flags; monitor authentication endpoints; enforce rollback procedures; conduct post-incident reviews.

original_source: Error responses across multiple Cloud products
symptoms: error responses across multiple Cloud products
failure_pattern: A misconfiguration in the authentication and user management service caused error responses that propagated to multiple Cloud products, leading to widespread authentication failures.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated configuration validation; add comprehensive health checks; enforce versioned deployments with rollback; increase monitoring and alerting for authentication errors; conduct regular incident drills

failure_pattern: During a maintenance window, a change caused Atlas to become unavailable, leading to downtime for multiple Atlassian services. The issue was identified and resolved within 23 minutes.

failure_pattern: A misconfiguration caused the authentication service to fail for users lacking Projects or Goals, leading to intermittent errors and error pages when redirecting to home.atlassian.com.
mitigation_principle: Implement comprehensive input validation; add fallback for missing data; monitor authentication flows; add automated tests for edge cases; enforce configuration checks before deployment

original_source: Unable to invite new users due to missing recaptcha token
failure_pattern: The invitation workflow attempted to validate a recaptcha token, but due to a misconfiguration the token was missing, causing the backend to reject invitations and produce intermittent errors for users.
mitigation_principle: Validate third‑party integration configurations; implement health checks for external dependencies; add automated tests for recaptcha flow; monitor token generation and error rates; enforce graceful degradation when external services fail

original_source: Customers may experience delays or failures receiving emails
failure_pattern: A failure in the third‑party email delivery provider caused the outgoing email service to become degraded, leading to delayed or failed email notifications across multiple Atlassian products.
mitigation_principle: Implement health checks and circuit breakers for third‑party email services; add retry logic with exponential backoff; monitor email delivery metrics; set up alerting for latency thresholds; maintain redundancy with multiple SMTP providers; perform regular failover testing

original_source: Degraded experience adding and accessing media attachments
failure_pattern: A misconfiguration in the media storage service caused increased latency and timeouts when uploading or retrieving attachments, leading to degraded experience for API and signup endpoints.
mitigation_principle: 1. Implement automated health checks for media storage; 2. Add circuit breaker for media uploads; 3. Monitor latency thresholds; 4. Add fallback to local storage; 5. Review configuration changes with peer review

original_source: Degraded performance to multiple Atlassian experiences
failure_pattern: A faulty CDN configuration change introduced an invalid hostname, causing TLS handshake failures and HTTP 503/403 errors for Atlassian services; the issue persisted until the change was rolled back, after which services gradually recovered.
mitigation_principle: Implement stricter pre-deployment validation for CDN configurations; enforce immutable hostname rules; use sharding for progressive deployment; add automated tests to detect hostname conflicts; enable automated rollback on validation failure

failure_pattern: An outage in AWS disrupted Atlassian's cloud services, causing cascading failures across API, integrations, authentication, and user management, leading to widespread service disruptions for customers.
mitigation_principle: Implement multi-cloud redundancy; add health checks and automated failover; monitor third-party provider status and set up alerts; establish clear SLAs and incident response playbooks; use circuit breakers and rate limiting; diversify dependencies across providers.
